goal: Samuel Campbell's résumé site as a pure-text experience: every line rains down from the top and locks into place, escorted by a swarm of tiny cursor drones (original, inspired by falling-code films and drone-swarm sci-fi; no film quotes, logos or names). Recruiters still get name/role/company/email immediately; content always renders from assets/resume-data.js and stays real, selectable, accessible text.
timeline_rules: Every evaluated round is snapshotted to versions/vNN/ and listed in versions/manifest.js. Turning points are featured. Visitors can open any version, step between milestones, and return to the current best in one action. Losing experiments stay in the archive.
design_spec: NEWDESIGNS.md section 'Direction 3: Text Rain' (this run). Cockpit spec above it is kept for history.

history.title: Three concepts
history.lesson: Content model is solid; the front door is a chooser.

history.title: The Learning Curve
history.lesson: One strong interaction beats a menu. Drag, keyboard, rail and hold-taps all work. Weak spots: CLS 0.10 on desktop from font swap, chalk bag clips mid-row, the bag change is instant so the skill story is easy to miss.

history.title: Skills you can watch pile up
history.lesson: Motion that carries meaning works: chips make the curve's y-axis legible. Kept it cheap (WAAPI, no library) and fully skipped under reduced motion. On phones the summit CTA duplicated the main buttons, so it shrinks to just Copy address.

history.title: Spotlight a skill, share the view
history.lesson: Making the rack a filter for the wall connects the below-the-fold content to the hero. Found and fixed a race: the idle hint was yanking the token back after a spotlight. Long unbroken tokens in bullets needed overflow-wrap on phones.

history.title: Patch Bay (alternate direction)
history.lesson: A puzzle in front of the facts slows recruiters, and a matrix of 32 cables is less legible than one spotlight. The 'NO CARRIER: COBOL lives at …' microcopy is worth stealing for the spotlight. The Learning Curve stays the foundation.

history.title: Round two & the 99% send
history.lesson: Specific beats generic. The floating badge crowds the narrow phone route, so on phones the 99% moves into the card instead. Measuring CLS sources showed the real culprit was late-filled text in a centered grid, not fonts.

history.title: Scrub the register
history.lesson: Previews make the archive worth visiting. Lazy-loading the iframe only when the section is on screen kept the home page light, and embedded previews skip their own register to avoid nesting.

history.title: Pull a Print (alternate direction)
history.lesson: Typography and one-job-per-page pacing are the zine's real wins. The pull is delightful but hides essentials. Rapid page flips needed a pending-target fix. Worth merging: a calm pitch-by-pitch reading mode for the résumé section.

history.title: Phone-first: the curve on its side
history.lesson: Designing for the thumb beat shrinking the desktop. Separating horizontal-scrub from vertical-scroll intent (8px, dominant axis) was essential; tested with real touch events. On a phone the horizontal curve reads even more like a learning curve than the vertical climb.

history.title: Pitches, borrowed from the zine
history.lesson: Borrowing one idea from a losing direction strengthened the winner. Testing print with a real PDF exposed that the first check had been rendered in screen mode by mistake; under print media it went 3 → 2 pages after trimming the intro.

history.title: climb --help & belay check
history.lesson: Hidden layers add delight at near-zero cost to the main path. Native <dialog> gave focus trap + Esc for free. The belay zones made the drag snapping logic visible, which is useful for tuning too.

history.title: Pitch bar navigation
history.lesson: A persistent section index is worth its 56px on phones. The bigger win was the bug it surfaced: test fixed elements after scrolling, not just at load. Also fixed: rack chip rows were not wrapping on phones since v1.

history.title: Compare any version with the summit
history.lesson: Side-by-side previews make 'why it changed' land faster than prose. Scaling two 1280px iframes into half-width boxes stays sharp enough to read headings.

history.title: Night climb
history.lesson: Keeping the paper cards made the dark theme feel like the same site. Caught a CSS gotcha: a background shorthand with a color in a non-final layer is invalid and silently dropped; measured contrast exposed it immediately.

history.title: Auto-belay (watch it climb)
history.lesson: A guided mode complements rather than duplicates when it adds information (the captions). Same trap as v5's knot: buttons inside the route must be excluded from drag-start. On phones, caption placement needed the empty lower-right of the curve so it never covers holds.

history.title: Works offline
history.lesson: Network-first for everything is the safe default for a site that changes every round; cache-first assets would have paired fresh HTML with stale JS after deploys. The size budget is now the clearest technical debt: the night theme and accumulated features doubled the CSS.

history.title: Weight diet (regression-tested)
history.lesson: Cruft was small; features are the weight. A standing regression suite (one action script per round) made the cleanup safe, and it's now the gate for every future round. Remaining budget gap (~86381 vs 60000 bytes uncompressed, ~25KB gzipped) is recorded as known debt.

history.title: One site, many rooms
history.lesson: Consistent wayfinding is cheap and makes the modes feel like part of one site. Inside archived snapshots, links to the register must escape the snapshot folder; the bar now detects that.

history.title: Share card
history.lesson: The first impression extends to places the site doesn't control. The OG image is a snapshot of data, so it must be regenerated when the résumé changes (documented in tools/og-card.html).

history.title: Cockpit: Frame AUTODIDACT
history.lesson: The install log maps onto the data with zero invention: contact counts equal the cumulative skill count at every sortie, verified going up and down. CLS needed three fixes: reserved space for JS-filled readouts, transform-only throttle movement, and a console with fixed line slots instead of appended rows.

history.title: Target lock + cold start
history.lesson: Lock-on makes the skills data part of the cockpit instead of a list. Honest edge case: untagged skills (Kentico, WordPress) say 'listed in the system bays, not tied to one sortie' rather than faking a location. The boot is opacity-only so CLS stays 0.

history.title: Sensor Scope (alternate direction)
history.lesson: A map shows everything at once but tells no story; the throttle's sequence is what makes learning feel like progress. Worth keeping: tap-to-ping as a playful way to lock contacts on the cockpit's own scope.

history.title: Story refits
history.lesson: Set pieces make specific facts stick. The decode stays reflow-free by overlaying an absolutely positioned scramble on transparent real text, so screen readers only ever get the real text and the box never resizes. Borrowing the rejected v21's ping worked well.

history.title: Sound, reference card, overdrive
history.lesson: Opt-in sound with zero audio until the first gesture keeps the page polite. The throttle-slam trigger needed loosening (3 extremes, not 4) to be findable by hand.

history.title: Service Log & archived frames
history.lesson: Consistent naming and palette across every page makes the redesign feel complete. Known issue noticed: the git-log room has its own layout shift on load (unchanged since v0).

history.title: Hangar Refit (alternate direction)
history.lesson: Scrolling is the easiest navigation, but 'fun' in this brief means hands-on control. Worth merging: one crate per installed system on the frame schematic is a more satisfying counter than per-bay hardpoints.

history.title: Mission briefings + crate frame
history.lesson: A focused, shareable per-job view helps recruiters who want one role in detail. Hash-change navigation needed the same briefing handling as a fresh load. Crates per system make the frame a truthful progress bar.

history.title: Pilot record (achievements)
history.lesson: Hints in the record double as a discovery guide for the hidden features. Guarded 'Full systems' so the 6-second autopilot can't award it.

history.title: Controller linked
history.lesson: Edge-triggered buttons plus a continuous stick that settles on release feels right. Verified with a simulated gamepad (axes and buttons injected); real hardware is untested.

history.title: Loadout screen
history.lesson: Provenance ('arrived in sortie 4, used in 4') answers both 'what' and 'how deep' at a glance. Untagged skills honestly say 'on file'.

history.title: Hangar day
history.lesson: Theme tokens made the light variant mostly a palette swap; the exceptions were hard-coded dark surfaces and text on amber/green fills. An automated contrast audit (~150 elements per theme) is now part of the suite.

history.title: Text Rain + drone escort
history.lesson: Measuring each word with Range rects lets the canvas land glyphs exactly where the DOM text sits, so the hand-off is seamless. Drones needed easing (swoop, then ride) to read as a swarm rather than markers. Hero lands in ~1.1–1.4 s.

history.title: The swarm comes alive
history.lesson: Wrapping the clicked word in a temporary span (then unwrapping and normalizing) lets the canvas scramble it without touching layout; verified the text is identical afterwards. Sampling the handle from an offscreen canvas gives a formation for any handle without a hand-made pixel font.

history.title: Résumé REPL (alternate direction)
history.lesson: Commands are great for precise questions ('where did he use Drupal?') but bad as the only way in. Keep the document; borrow the find-a-skill answer for a type-to-find feature on it.

history.title: Type to find (swarm-assisted)
history.lesson: Borrowing the REPL's best idea onto the document beat the REPL itself. Moved the drone hive to the bottom-right so it no longer covers the header controls.

history.title: Channel switching
history.lesson: Re-raining the destination turns navigation into part of the show at almost no cost (it reuses the entrance engine in quick mode). Phones still lack a section index; that's a gap to fill.

history.title: Cheap enough to keep
history.lesson: Decorative idle motion is the usual reason an animation loop never stops. The remaining hitch is measurement of big sections at once; chunking that is a candidate for a later round.

history.title: Drone carry
history.lesson: A first pass moved every word on its own arc and dissolved into a word cloud; carrying each block as one unit with a visible four-drone squad reads as 'the swarm is moving this'. Staggering blocks 120 ms apart keeps the paths readable.

history.title: Swarm Board
history.lesson: Reusing the measure-mutate-fly engine made a whole layout change cost almost nothing: anything the DOM can do, the swarm can animate. The board stays opt-in because the document is still faster to scan.

history.title: Recall
history.lesson: Shift+R clashed with type-to-find (capital letters start a search), so replay moved to 0, next to the 1–4 channel keys. Lift words need their glyph arrays initialised like falling ones.

history.title: Gather
history.lesson: getComputedStyle is live: read the colour before adding the class that hides the target, or the flying copy is invisible. The find bar needed flex-wrap so the list sits under the input instead of squeezing it.

history.title: Phosphor repaint
history.lesson: The sweep only reads as 'drones painting' when the drone row and the wipe use the same timing: start the drones on viewTransition.ready, and use linear motion for both. All four schemes pass AA on 95 checked elements.

history.title: Dispatch
history.lesson: The tag line shifts every word in a matched card, so cards scatter a little more mid-flight than plain sorts do; the result settles cleanly. Skills that aren't tagged on any role get an honest note instead of an empty carry.

history.title: Text changelog
history.lesson: The archive bar is a single script that every snapshot loads, so restyling it updates all 43 archived versions at once. On phones it now sits above the bottom nav instead of covering the header.

history.title: Hive orders
history.lesson: The skip button stays visible until every block has rained (often never on long pages), so hiding the hive while skip showed hid it almost permanently. Moving skip to the left on phones fixed the overlap instead.

history.title: Ambient rain
history.lesson: Capping it at about 20 fps and stopping on idle keeps the cost negligible (frames stay at 60 with a worst frame of 17 ms). Damping it to 40% inside the reading column was what made it atmosphere rather than noise.

history.title: Hail relay
history.lesson: Reserving the button width keeps '[ copy ]' → '[ copied ]' from shifting the line. Splitting the address into six-character chunks reads better than one long string flying.

history.title: Ship-shape
history.lesson: The share card renders from the same resume-data.js as the page, so it can't drift from the résumé (it caught a wrong field name on the first render).

history.title: Final polish
history.lesson: Two skills share a name across groups (SQL appears under Languages and under Data & Messaging). Dispatch handles that fine, but it's worth a tidy-up in resume-data.js.

history.title: Swarm build
history.lesson: Drones that went straight back to the hive after the huddle made the build look like it started from a corner. Holding them in place for a moment lets the nearest drones claim the first elements straight from the centre.

history.title: Motion switch
history.lesson: Respecting reduced motion silently can look like a broken site to its own owner. Say what's happening and let the visitor choose.

history.title: Built by swarm-intro
history.lesson: Phones fire height-only resize events as the address bar slides, and the old 'skip on resize' rule killed the intro on mobile. Now only width changes skip it. The library's own reduced-motion check is turned off so our motion switch is the single source of truth.

history.title: Tractor mode
history.lesson: The text is still real and in the page while it's drawn as grass, so find, copy and screen readers keep working. Mowing is what makes the mode usable as well as funny.

history.title: Tractor fixes + visible swarm button
history.lesson: Hiding text by setting color: transparent breaks anything that inherits its colour. text-fill-color leaves the real colours intact. And the reduced-motion path needs its own visual check, not just a functional one.

history.title: Text becomes grass
history.lesson: Blades sized to the type: big headings get long, lush blades, while small text gets fewer, shorter ones so it stays readable. Phones fire resize events as the address bar moves, and rebuilding the field then orphaned every tractor, so rebuilds now only happen on width changes and release the tractors.

history.title: Growth stages
history.lesson: Randomising each letter's start (up to 0.4 s) and speed (±25%) did more for 'organic' than any single blade detail.

history.title: Cut turf
history.lesson: Depth helps big type and hurts small type. Merging (turf for headings, flat for body) beat either pure version side by side.

history.title: Drawn tractors
history.lesson: Size matters more than detail: a 2.4× tractor on the 64 px name reads instantly, while 20 px tractors there looked like specks.

history.title: Lawn care
history.lesson: Stripe bands keyed to page x (every 14 px), not to letters, line up across lines and read as one lawn.

history.title: Quiet lawn
history.lesson: A hidden canvas isn't a stopped canvas. The ambient rain's loop had to check for tractor mode itself.

history.title: The field
history.lesson: Two furrow rhythms (11 px and 37 px) stop the soil reading as lined paper.

history.title: Fieldwork
history.lesson: Choosing the start end by proximity was enough to create serpentine rows naturally; no explicit route planning was needed.

history.title: Rain
history.lesson: Keeping growth as a single 'lushness' multiplier on blade length meant no rebuild was needed: the existing blades simply stretch.

history.title: Drive it yourself
history.lesson: Keys had to be captured before the type-to-find handler (capture phase + stopImmediatePropagation); otherwise WASD opened search.

history.title: Touch the grass
history.lesson: A slower release (12% per frame) than push (35%) is what makes it read as springy rather than glued to the cursor.

history.title: Tractor regression + first-time tip
history.lesson: No breakages this time. Running the shared regression after each round in this cycle kept problems from piling up.

history.title: Wildflowers
history.lesson: Flowers only open in the last fifth of a blade's growth, so they arrive as a payoff after the grass is up rather than cluttering the sprout stage.

history.title: Tractor toolbox
history.lesson: Icon-only works on phones because the first-time tip maps each icon to its word once.

history.title: Sound (opt-in)
history.lesson: Headless tests can confirm the toggle and audio graph start without errors, but not how it sounds. It needs a listen on a real machine.

history.title: Phone performance
history.lesson: Fill calls weren't the whole cost. Letter bodies and soil strips are a big share too, so further gains would come from caching fully grown words as bitmaps.

history.title: Documented + verified
history.lesson: Inside archived snapshots Esc means 'back to current', so the verifier must not press Esc as part of a feature test.

history.title: Tidy barn + run wrap-up
history.lesson: Fixed parking slots also make the idle loop settle sooner, because tractors stop jittering around a shared point.

history.title: Mow to reveal
history.lesson: The first version mowed the whole screen in about a second. The field needs a held beat and slower tractors (0.9 px/ms) to read as tractors at work rather than a wipe transition.

history.title: Swarm mows the text
history.lesson: Fast scrolling could jump a line from below the screen to above it between frames, so it never got queued and the intro never finished. Lines are now queued once they've been reached at all, whether they're on screen or already past.

owner_feedback.text: Run of cycles/rounds on tractor/grass mode. Grass is very basic: make it seem like it's really growing, not a 2D line upward. The text should BE the grass (not text under grass). Tractors should erase the text when clicked (mowing). When the page loads, tractors go out and till the area, growing the text grass.
On page load the whole page should look like a massive field of grass; the tractor swarm mows the entire page so the website text can be seen.
Didn't like v72's grass-cover animation; wants the swarm to mow the text itself (each element mowed into view).
